title: Privilege Constellation Trellis: workspace permission map and audit flows
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Problem: Admins and security reviewers struggle to understand who has access across nested workspaces and how rollouts change permission surface area. Existing audit log views are linear and noisy; product and infra teams need a consolidated visual that connects roles, temporal changes, cost implications, and rollout policies.

Goal: Design a compact, scannable console surface — the 'Privilege Constellation Trellis' — that visualizes role bindings, permission inheritance, recent grant/revoke events, rollout state (canary/gradual/all), and estimated cost impact for role changes. The surface should support quick access reviews, bulk remediation flows, and direct links to audit log entries and policy diffs.

Scope: Workspace & org-level RBAC surface, role composition inspector, timeline scrubber for access changes, cost snapshot for role-wide token usage, and an access-review workflow prototype. Excludes: identity provider configuration (SSO), low-level KMS/HSM logs.

User stories:
- As a security reviewer, I want to see all users with 'model.deploy' across a workspace and related sub-workspaces, with the ability to filter by role and by recent activity.
- As an admin, I want to preview the impact of revoking a role (users removed, dashboards affected, tokens impacted) before applying changes.
- As a product manager, I want to link permission rollouts to release toggles and see cost delta estimates for high-cost roles.

Success criteria: Reduced mean time to detect privileged drift during audits by 35% in pilot orgs; at least 2/3 of reviewers prefer the Trellis over the baseline audit list in usability testing.
acceptance_criteria: Trellis renders role-to-actor graph for selected workspace with <1s initial load on test data (10k nodes simulated)
Clicking a role node opens an inspector with membership list, recent grant/revoke events (linked to audit entries), and cost estimate for role activity
Access review flow: select users/roles -> propose change -> simulate impact -> submit for approval (flows to existing approvals queue)
Export/Link: every node/event has a permalink to the audit log and a GitHub-style permalink for the change diff
prototypes: Figma - Role Inspector (frame: Trellis - Role Inspector)
Figma - Access Review Modal (frame: Trellis - Access Review)
Clickable HTML prototype hosted at https://staging.redwood.com/trellis-proto
decisions: Use a compact node-link trellis with temporal scrubber rather than a full adjacency matrix to prioritize discoverability over completeness
Cost estimates will be computed from token-level attribution aggregated per-role (backend will supply an API) rather than on-the-fly full-query for performance
Default view shows inferred least-privilege suggestions via heuristics; these suggestions are 'view-only' until a reviewer promotes them to remediation proposals

risk_mitigation: To avoid accidental mass revokes, bulk actions default to 'simulate' mode and require a two-step approval for >25 affected accounts. Role changes are never applied until backend validation returns a non-empty token-attribution snapshot.
accessibility_considerations: Colorblind-safe palette for node states, keyboard navigation for trellis exploration, dynamically sized nodes with aria labels that include role name, actor count, and last change timestamp
QA_notes: QA should validate performance with synthetic graph payloads (1k nodes, 5k edges; 10k nodes simulated load tests handled by mock server)
Verify permalinks open the correct audit log entry and that simulated revokes produce deterministic impact reports
